newsitem.title: USA: Visa denies AmEx's anti-competitive claim in Chile.
newsitem.headline: Visa denies AmEx's anti-competitive claim in Chile.

text.p: Visa said on Thursday that allegations by American Express Co that it had engaged in anti-competitive practices in Chile were "totally false".

"Visa has not restricted banks from issuing cards with other brands," Clive Edwards, Visa's vice president for the Latin American region and general manager in Chile, told Reuters. "The allegations are totally false."
American Express filed a legal complaint against Visa in Chile, alleging the company limited competition by restricting the products its member banks could offer.
American Express previously filed similar complaints against Visa in Argentina, Mexico, Brazil, Colombia and Puerto Rico. Visa denied these allegations on September 24.

"Twenty-thousand banks around the world own Visa. They make decisions concerning business in general. American Express is taking action against the banks with whom it hopes to do business," said Edwards, who added that Visa was surprised by the complaints in Chile.
Visa was also not planning to discuss potential product restrictions on its banks at an October 10 board meeting, Edwards said.
"The issue is not on the agenda and was not on the agenda before American Express filed the complaints," he said.
